fields.Trigger: PO receipt where actual price ≠ standard; monthly variance review

Automation Opportunity: - Auto PPV capture at receipt; threshold-based vendor alerts; PPV-to-roll feed
Controls: - CTL-705 (ensure controlled execution — Cost Variance, Actual-vs-Standard & Margin Analytics (PA-158.2).)
- CTL-705: PPV captured at every receipt; unfavorable variances > threshold routed and reviewed; PPV feeds the standard roll
Cross-references: - links to VS-03/VS-67 (vendor/scorecard), W4656 (roll), W4661 (margin), VS-17.1 (GL)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unaddressed-PPV risk**: Persistent unfavorable PPV on a vendor not acted on erodes margin silently; mitigated by threshold-based routing to Procurement
- **Standard-lag risk**: Standard not updated to reflect persistent PPV accumulates large revaluations; mitigated by feeding PPV into the roll
System Touchpoints: - PO receipt (VS-04); PPV ledger; vendor scorecard (VS-67); analytics (VS-28); GL (VS-17.1)

steps.activity: Capture PPV at every receipt (actual purchase price − standard cost); post to the PPV P&L account and accumulate by vendor/category/SKU
Analyze PPV monthly: favorable vs. unfavorable by vendor/category; route unfavorable variances exceeding threshold to Procurement/Vendor Mgmt for vendor accountability and negotiation (VS-03.3/VS-67)
Feed recurring PPV into the next standard-cost roll (W4656) so the standard reflects the new actual; track PPV trend as a procurement-KPI input (VS-67 scorecard)

fields.Trigger: Import landed-cost finalization (W4651); monthly variance review

workflows.name: Landed-Cost Variance vs. Standard & Import Rate Volatility Analysis

Automation Opportunity: - Variance decomposition engine; volatility-vs-hedge dashboard; freight/FX-index feed
Controls: - CTL-705 (ensure controlled execution — Cost Variance, Actual-vs-Standard & Margin Analytics (PA-158.2).)
- CTL-705: landed-cost variance decomposed by element; volatility vs. hedge quantified monthly; variance feeds the roll and commodity decisions
Cross-references: - links to W4651 (landed cost), VS-106 (commodity), VS-18.3 (FX), VS-110/VS-87 (freight/duty), W4656 (roll)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unhedged-exposure risk**: Import FX/freight volatility not quantified vs. the hedge → surprise margin hits; mitigated by the volatility-vs-hedge analysis
- **Demurrage leakage risk**: Recurring demurrage/detention (W249) inflating landed cost without corrective action; mitigated by variance decomposition and routing to VS-110
System Touchpoints: - Landed-cost module (W4651); freight audit (VS-110.3); FX/treasury (VS-18.3); commodity (VS-106); GL (VS-17.1)

steps.activity: Compare actual landed cost (W4651) to standard landed cost; decompose the variance into freight, duty, brokerage, insurance, demurrage, and FX components; post to the appropriate variance accounts
Analyze import-rate volatility (ocean freight rates, FX, commodity-linked duty) vs. the commodity/FX hedge posture (VS-106/VS-18.3); quantify unhedged exposure and pass-through adequacy (VS-106.3)
Feed landed-cost variance into the standard roll (W4656) and into commodity-risk decisions (VS-106); recommend forward-buy/hedging/duty-optimization actions (VS-87/VS-110/VS-106)

fields.Trigger: Kit assembly / build-to-order (VS-92); monthly variance review

workflows.name: Production / Conversion Variance for Kitting & Build-to-Order

Automation Opportunity: - Auto variance capture at assembly; yield/efficiency dashboards by kit/DC
Controls: - CTL-705 (ensure controlled execution — Cost Variance, Actual-vs-Standard & Margin Analytics (PA-158.2).)
- CTL-705: conversion variance captured and decomposed; yield/efficiency drivers routed; variance feeds the kit roll
Cross-references: - links to VS-92 (kitting), VS-04 (DC), W4653/W4654 (catch-weight/kit cost), VS-92.3 (economics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Yield-loss risk**: Component yield/scrap higher than standard erodes kit margin; mitigated by usage-variance analysis and yield re-verification (W4653)
- **Labor-efficiency risk**: Inefficient assembly inflates conversion cost; mitigated by efficiency-variance routing to DC ops
System Touchpoints: - DC kitting module (VS-92.2); conversion-variance ledger; GL (VS-17.1); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Capture conversion variance: actual assembly labor/overhead + component consumption vs. the kit standard cost (W4654); post material-usage and labor-rate/efficiency variances
Analyze conversion variance by kit/DC: identify yield loss, component substitution, and labor-efficiency drivers; route to DC operations for corrective action
Feed conversion variance into the kit-standard roll (W4654) and into kitting-economics decisions (VS-92.3)

fields.Trigger: Inventory adjustment (VS-05); shrinkage (VS-23); NRV review at close (W9)

workflows.name: Inventory Adjustment, Write-Down & NRV Cost Impact

Automation Opportunity: - Adjustment-to-cost-account auto-classification; SLOB/NRV candidate list with suggested provision; trend dashboards
Controls: - CTL-705 (ensure controlled execution — Cost Variance, Actual-vs-Standard & Margin Analytics (PA-158.2).)
- CTL-705: adjustments classified per rules; NRV reviewed each close (W9); inventory cost reconciled to GL
Cross-references: - links to VS-05/VS-23 (inventory/shrink), W220 (SLOB), W9 (close/NRV), VS-05.3 (disposition), W4663 (COGS recon)
Pain Points / Risks: - **NRV-miss risk**: Failing to write down SLOB to NRV overstates inventory and assets — audit finding; mitigated by the per-close NRV review
- **Mis-classified-adjustment risk**: A shrinkage write-off booked as a variance distorts margin; mitigated by the cost-account classification rules
System Touchpoints: - Inventory module (VS-05); shrinkage (VS-23); SLOB (W220); NRV review (W9); GL (VS-17.1)

steps.activity: Post the cost impact of inventory adjustments (shrinkage, damage, count variances — VS-05.1/VS-23) to the correct cost account (write-off vs. variance) using the current standard cost
At each close (W9), perform the lower-of-cost-or-NRV review (PFRS/IAS 2): identify slow-moving/obsolete stock (W220), estimate NRV vs. carrying cost, and book the write-down provision
Reconcile total inventory cost to the GL inventory account and the WAC verification (W9); analyze write-down trend and feed into assortment/SLOB decisions (VS-05.3)

workflows.name: Gross-Margin, MMU/IMU & Maintained-Margin Analytics by SKU / Category / Store

Automation Opportunity: - Margin/GMROI auto-computation; outlier-detection with cost-data validation; routing to pricing/merchandising
Controls: - CTL-705 (ensure controlled execution — Cost Variance, Actual-vs-Standard & Margin Analytics (PA-158.2).)
- CTL-705: margin pack cost-data-validated; outliers routed; aggregate tied to PFRS financials
Cross-references: - elevates W85 (VS-17.4); links to VS-01.2/VS-101/VS-64 (pricing/markdown), VS-28 (analytics), VS-17.4 (FP&A)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cost-data-error mis-signal risk**: Acting on a margin signal caused by a cost-master error (not a real margin problem) → bad pricing decisions; mitigated by cost-data validation before action
- **GMROI-blind risk**: Margin % without turn (GMROI) mis-ranks SKU productivity; mitigated by GMROI inclusion
System Touchpoints: - Margin analytics (VS-28/VS-17.4); cost layer (W4649); promo/markdown (VS-01.2/VS-64); merchandise FP (VS-101)
Time Estimate: - ~5–7 days/month margin analytics pack (elevates W85's margin-review scope)

steps.activity: Produce the margin analytics pack: gross margin % (net sales − COGS), initial markup (IMU), maintained markup (MMU) after markdowns, and GMROI by SKU/category/store/region/entity — using the cost layer (W4649/W4656) net of vendor funding (W4664)

Identify margin outliers (below category floor, eroding trend, store-specific) and route to Merchandising/Pricing for action (VS-01.2/VS-101/VS-64 markdown); validate cost-data accuracy before acting on a margin signal
Tie aggregate margin to the PFRS financials and the merchandise-financial plan (VS-101); feed maintained-margin into OTB and pricing strategy (VS-101/VS-01.2)

fields.Trigger: Monthly freight/duty cost review; vendor compliance chargeback decisions

workflows.name: Freight, Duty & Handling Cost Absorption vs. Billback Analysis

Automation Opportunity: - Compliance-event-to-chargeback auto-flag; absorb-vs-billback dashboards; recovery-rate tracking
Controls: - CTL-705 (ensure controlled execution — Cost Variance, Actual-vs-Standard & Margin Analytics (PA-158.2).)
- CTL-705: inbound cost classified absorb vs. billback; chargebacks evidence-based; unrecovered leakage quantified and routed
Cross-references: - links to W4651/W4652 (landed/domestic freight), W245 (chargeback), VS-110 (freight), VS-67 (scorecard)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Absorbed-leakage risk**: Vendor-compliance cost absorbed into COGS instead of recovered erodes margin; mitigated by the billback classification and recovery
- **Chargeback-dispute risk**: Chargebacks disputed by vendors without documentation → non-recovery; mitigated by evidence-based chargebacks (routing-guide compliance VS-110.2)
System Touchpoints: - Freight audit/pay (VS-110.3); vendor compliance chargeback (W245); landed cost (W4651); vendor scorecard (VS-67)

steps.activity: Classify inbound freight/duty/handling cost as absorbed (into SKU cost per W4651/W4652) vs. billback-eligible (vendor non-compliance — wrong carrier, late shipment, packaging non-conformance per W245)
Bill back vendor-compliance-eligible cost (W245 chargebacks) and recover; analyze the absorb-vs-billback posture for net cost optimization (renegotiate Incoterms, routing-guide compliance — VS-110.2)
Quantify unrecovered billback-eligible cost as margin leakage; route to vendor scorecard (VS-67) and freight-procurement (VS-110) for structural recovery

fields.Volume: ~PHP 42–45B annual COGS; ~ every POS/sales transaction + every receipt/adjustment

Automation Opportunity: - COGS-to-inventory-movement auto-reconciliation; cut-off-boundary flagging; entity/channel margin tie-out
Controls: - CTL-705: COGS reconciled to inventory movement monthly; cut-off tested; entity COGS tied to revenue and PFRS financials
Cross-references: - links to VS-05/VS-08 (inventory/POS), W9A (close), VS-72 (intercompany), W4661 (margin tie)
Pain Points / Risks: - **COGS-variance risk**: An unexplained COGS-to-inventory variance hides a costing/inventory error; mitigated by the monthly reconciliation and variance investigation
- **Cut-off risk**: Period-boundary sales/receipts mismatched to COGS → period margin distortion; mitigated by cut-off testing
System Touchpoints: - Inventory module (VS-05); POS sales (VS-08); GL (VS-17.1); month-end close (W9A); intercompany (VS-72)

steps.activity: Reconcile COGS to the inventory movement: opening inventory + receipts (at cost) + landed-cost adjustments − closing inventory = COGS; investigate any unexplained COGS variance
Perform COGS cut-off: ensure sales/shipments near period-end are matched to the corresponding COGS in the same period (and receipts in the correct period); clear cut-off exceptions
Reconcile COGS by entity/channel to revenue (margin tie-out) and to the PFRS financials; resolve any entity-allocation or intercompany COGS distortion (VS-72)

fields.Trigger: Markdown/promo run (VS-01.2/VS-64); vendor rebate/funding (VS-39); monthly review
fields.Volume: 6 major catalog promos/yr + monthly hot deals; vendor rebates (VS-39); co-op advertising

workflows.name: Markdown, Promo & Vendor-Funding Net-Cost Impact Accounting

Automation Opportunity: - Funding-classification rules engine; accrual-to-receipt auto-reconcile; unclaimed-funding alert
Controls: - CTL-705 (ensure controlled execution — Cost Variance, Actual-vs-Standard & Margin Analytics (PA-158.2).)
- CTL-705: vendor-funding accounting policy documented (no double-count); markdown accounted per policy; accrual reconciled to receipts monthly
Cross-references: - links to VS-39 (rebate), VS-01.2/VS-64/VS-58 (markdown/promo), W4661 (margin), W4638 (variable consideration)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Double-count risk**: Vendor funding netted against cost AND recorded as income (or missed) → margin distortion; mitigated by the documented netting policy and reconciliation
- **Unclaimed-funding risk**: Earned vendor rebates/funding not claimed → margin leakage; mitigated by the accrual-to-receipt reconciliation (VS-39.3)
System Touchpoints: - Markdown/promo module (VS-01.2/VS-64/VS-58); rebate accrual (VS-39); GL (VS-17.1); margin analytics (W4661)

steps.activity: Determine the correct accounting for vendor funding: reduction of cost of goods (net cost) vs. reduction of selling expense vs. other income — per PFRS and the documented policy; net rebates (VS-39) and co-op advertising against the funded SKU's cost
Account for markdown/promo cost: temporary vs. permanent markdown, markdown reserve, and the net margin impact after vendor funding; post the markdown to margin or a markdown P&L account per policy
Reconcile vendor-funding accrual (VS-39) to actual receipts and to the net-cost reduction claimed; identify unfunded/unclaimed vendor funding as recovery opportunity (VS-39.3)
